Buying guide

Pre-construction condos: what to check before you sign

You have ten days to back out. Here's what to check in them, what your deposit is protected for, and the costs that show up at occupancy.

Ali Bayat
Figures checked against the sources below on November 21, 2026
Published November 21, 2026
4-minute readOntario rulesUpdated November 2026
The short version
  • You can cancel a new condo purchase within 10 days of receiving the signed agreement and disclosure statement, for any reason.
  • Tarion protects condo deposits only up to $20,000. Ask how the rest is held.
  • During interim occupancy you pay a monthly fee, not a mortgage. Budget for it.

01Four numbers to know

10 daysCooling-off periodStarts once you have the signed agreement, disclosure statement and the Condo Buyers' Guide
$20,000Tarion deposit protectionFor condos; deposits must also be held in trust
30 daysTo walk away after a missed outside dateIf the builder misses the outside occupancy date
$80,000Max Ontario HST reliefNew homes, agreements signed Apr 1, 2026 to Mar 31, 2027, per CRA

02What happens, and when

  1. 01

    Sign and start the clock

    Day 0

    You sign, then receive the disclosure statement and the Condo Buyers' Guide. The 10 days start once you have all of them.

  2. 02

    Lawyer review

    Days 1–10

    Have a real estate lawyer read the agreement, the Statement of Critical Dates and the closing adjustments before day 10.

  3. 03

    Pay deposits

    Months 0–24

    Deposits are usually paid in instalments. Keep proof of every payment.

  4. 04

    Interim occupancy

    Building ready

    You move in and pay an occupancy fee: interest on the unpaid price, estimated property tax and estimated common expenses.

  5. 05

    Registration and final closing

    Months later

    The condo is registered, title transfers to you, your mortgage starts and closing adjustments are charged.

03Check these in your 10 days

  • The builder's recordLook it up in the HCRA Ontario Builder Directory: licence, warranty claims and cancelled projects.
  • Early termination conditionsWhen the builder can cancel, for example if not enough units sell or financing falls through.
  • Closing adjustmentsAsk for caps on development charges, utility hookups and other levies charged at closing.
  • Assignment clauseWhether you can sell before closing, the fee, and whether the builder must consent.
  • Occupancy fee estimateAsk for the expected monthly fee and how long occupancy usually lasts in their buildings.
  • Mortgage at closingYour lender appraises at closing, not at signing. If values fall, you cover the gap.

04Red flags

  • Uncapped leviesClosing costs with no upper limit can add thousands.
  • Deposits over $20,000 with no answer on how they're protectedAsk the builder's lawyer in writing.
  • Pressure to sign before you've read the disclosure statementThe 10 days exist for a reason.
  • A builder with past cancelled projectsCheck the directory before you sign, not after.

05Today's market context

In October 2026, GTA condo apartments sold for an average of $621,400, down 5.8% from a year earlier, per TRREB. A unit bought at the top of the market can appraise for less at closing, which is why the mortgage line in your checklist matters.

Ali's take

Read the closing adjustments schedule before anything else. That's where the surprise costs live, and it's the part buyers skip.

Quick answers

Can I cancel a pre-construction condo in Ontario?

Yes, within 10 days of receiving the signed agreement of purchase and sale, the disclosure statement and Ontario's Condo Buyers' Guide, without giving a reason. After that, you're generally bound by the agreement.

Is my pre-construction condo deposit protected?

Deposits must be held in trust, and Tarion protects up to $20,000 of a condo deposit if the builder doesn't return it. Ask how any amount above $20,000 is protected.

What is an interim occupancy fee?

A monthly fee you pay after moving in but before the condo is registered. It is capped at interest on the unpaid purchase price plus estimated property taxes and common expenses for the unit.

Looking at a pre-construction unit?

Send me the agreement and I'll walk you through the deposit schedule, adjustments and assignment terms before your 10 days run out.
